result.topic_en: Corollaries on the differential equation and boundary conditions required for the integral formula ∫Z dx to be a maximum or minimum, followed by the statement of Problem 2, in which Z also depends on another integral formula Φ = ∫ℨ dx.
result.transcription:
118 \quad DE METHODO

crementum extremi valoris ipſius $y$; at $d\delta y$, $dd\delta y$ etc. pendebunt inſuper ab incrementis valorum contiguorum.

Coroll. 1.

Si ergo formula integralis $\int Z dx$ debeat eſſe maximum vel minimum pro termino $x=a$, neceſſe eſt, vt eius variatio differentialis euaneſcat, quomodocunque variationes $\delta y$ accipiantur. Primum ergo oportet ſit, pro omnibus valoribus intermediis ipſius $x$,
$N-\frac{dP}{dx}+\frac{ddQ}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3R}{dx^3}+\frac{d^4S}{dx^4}-\text{etc.}=0$
qua aequatione relatio requiſita inter $x$ et $y$ continetur.

Coroll. 2.

Hinc autem, ſi termini P, Q, R etc. adſint, ob integrationes inſtituendas relatio inter $x$ et $y$ non penitus determinatur, quia in eam per ſingulas integrationes conſtantes quantitates arbitrariae ingrediuntur. His igitur caſibus ad quaeſtionem maximi vel minimi aliae nonnullae conditiones adiungi poſſunt, veluti vt pro datis quibusdam valoribus ipſius $x$, altera variabilis $y$ datos valores obtineat.

Coroll. 3.

Omiſſis autem huiusmodi conditionibus, noua quaeſtio formari poteſt, quemadmodum conſtantes illae per integrationem introductae definiri debeant, vt vel maximum maximorum vel minimum minimorum obtineatur: pro hoc autem neceſſe eſt, vt, poſito $x=a$, his aequationibus ſatisfiat:
$P-\frac{dQ}{dx}+\frac{ddR}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3S}{dx^3}=0$
$Q-\frac{dR}{dx}+\frac{ddS}{dx^2}=0$
$R-\frac{dS}{dx}=0$
$S=0$.

119 \quad MAXIMORVM ET MINIMORVM.

Coroll. 4.

Deinde vero ob easdem rationes opus eſt, vt pro altero termino $x=0$, iisdem hiſce aequationibus ſatisfiat. Nam cum variatio differentialis euaneſcere debeat poſito $x=0$, pars integralis eiusmodi conſtantem inuoluit, quae hanc conditionem adimpleat; haec autem conſtans terminos abſolutos, ſi in iis ponatur $x=0$, ad nihilum redigere debet. Quare formulae illae:
$P-\frac{dQ}{dx}+\frac{ddR}{dx^2}-\text{etc.}\quad Q-\frac{dR}{dx}+\text{etc.}\quad R-\frac{dS}{dx}\text{ etc.}$
aeque euaneſcere debent caſu $x=0$, atque caſu $x=a$.

Problema 2.

Si functio Z praeter quantitates $x, y, p, q, r$ etc. etiam formulam quandam integralem $\Phi=\int \mathfrak{Z}\, dx$ vtcunque implicet, vt ſit
$dZ=L\,d\Phi+M\,dx+N\,dy+P\,dp+Q\,dq+R\,dr+S\,ds$ etc.
in formula autem $\Phi$ ſit $\mathfrak{Z}$ functio quaecunque ipſarum $x, y, p, q, r$ etc. exiſtente
$d\mathfrak{Z}=\mathfrak{M}\,dx+\mathfrak{N}\,dy+\mathfrak{P}\,dp+\mathfrak{Q}\,dq+\mathfrak{R}\,dr+\mathfrak{S}\,ds$ etc.
atque his ita ſe habentibus, oporteat definiri variationem differentialem huius formulae integralis $\int Z dx$, a termino $x=0$ ad terminum $x=a$ extenſam.

Solutio.

items.english: First, therefore, it is necessary that for all intermediate values of x, N − dP/dx + d²Q/dx² − d³R/dx³ + d⁴S/dx⁴ − etc. = 0.

items.english: A new question can be formed: how the constants introduced by integration should be determined so that either the maximum of maxima or the minimum of minima is obtained.

items.english: If the function Z, besides the quantities x, y, p, q, r etc., also involves in any way some integral formula Φ = ∫ℨ dx, so that dZ = L dΦ + M dx + N dy + P dp + Q dq + R dr + S ds etc., and in the formula Φ, ℨ is any function of x, y, p, q, r etc. with dℨ = 𝔐 dx + 𝔑 dy + 𝔓 dp + 𝔔 dq + ℜ dr + 𝔖 ds etc.; with matters so arranged, the differential variation of the integral formula ∫Z dx, extended from the limit x = 0 to the limit x = a, is to be determined.
